newsitem.title: USA: Refiner buying, pipeline cuts keep US grades firm.
newsitem.headline: Refiner buying, pipeline cuts keep US grades firm.

text.p: Refiners stepped-up buying Monday ahead of pipeline throughput reductions and before September business ends late week.

Outright prices faltered on the NYMEX screen due to profit-taking and soft unleaded gasoline values. Benchmark September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing lost around 15 cents a barrel by late session, talked at $19.85-95 a barrel.
September NYMEX futures expire on Wednesday, leaving pipeline scheduling for Friday. Cash dealers said major refiners came into the sour domestic market this morning looking to fill needs.
"They were short, so they came in looking for some crude," said a cash trader.

In addition to active refiner demand, sour barrels gained on Chicago-area refiners buying before cuts on IPL's Interprovincial Pipe Line system take effect in September. Some 140,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude throughput to the U.S. Midwest is to be cut due to maintenance.
"Sour was pretty strong this morning. People are still trying to find out what's going on with IPL," a Gulf buyer said, noting the role Chicago refiners played on the uptick.
Competing pipelines, notably Arco's 250,000 bpd capacity Seaway line from the U.S. Gulf to the Midwest are able to handle flows that normally come from Canada, operator Arco said through a spokesman.

Still, the Canada cuts and the buying sprees pushed West Texas Sour/Midland to differentials at WTI -$1.10, before selling stalled and the grade moved back to a $1.15-25 discount late in the session, 10 cents stronger than Friday.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James ended around 23-25 cents over the marker, and Midland/WTI at a slightly firmer 28-26 cents discount, traders said.

Outright prices failed to find much news for moving prices, though expectations for the normal return of Tosco's catalytic cracker at the Bayway refinery in Linden, New Jersey, helped to deflate the energy complex.

There was also no significant development on Iraq Monday, save the fact an ultra-large oil tanker docked at the Mina al-Bakr terminal for loading 2.2 million barrels of crude under U.N. oil-for-food terms.
